title: Consumer Outcomes and Conduct Risk for Firms
summary: A ten-module programme giving firms the tools to design, test and evidence good customer outcomes and manage conduct risk across the customer journey.
intro: This training programme equips compliance, risk, product and customer-facing managers to design, test and evidence good customer outcomes and manage conduct risk, seeing the firm's customers the way a supervisor does.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip the people who design products, serve customers and oversee conduct with the frameworks and tools to deliver and evidence good outcomes for retail customers. Participants leave able to test products, value, communications and support against outcomes, act on what the data shows and report credibly to the board and supervisors.
sections.What It Covers: Product governance, fair value, communications and disclosure, vulnerable customers, sales and advice, complaints and root cause analysis, outcomes testing and management information, conduct risk frameworks, culture and incentives, and board reporting.
Intended Audience: Compliance, conduct risk and consumer outcome specialists
Product, marketing, pricing and customer service managers
Senior managers and business-line owners accountable for retail customer outcomes
Learning Objectives: Explain how conduct risk arises and why supervisors focus on outcomes rather than process
Design product governance and fair value assessments that withstand scrutiny
Apply outcome testing to communications, sales, advice and customer support
Identify and support customers in vulnerable circumstances
Evaluate complaints, root causes and management information to find and fix customer harm
Produce conduct risk reporting that supports board challenge and agree an action plan for the firm
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines practical tools with case studies, data exercises and group discussion, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of compliance, product or customer-facing work in a retail financial services firm is helpful. No specialist conduct background is required.
Core Reading: G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
World Bank, Good Practices for Financial Consumer Protection (2017)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)

modules.title: Conduct Risk and the Outcomes-Based Approach
modules.summary: Why supervisors have moved from rules-based compliance to testing real outcomes for customers, and what that means for the firm's governance and control functions.
objectives: Explain the drivers of conduct risk and customer harm
Distinguish outcome-based supervision from process compliance
Identify where the firm's business model creates conduct risk
syllabus: Conduct risk: definition, drivers and harm
From disclosure to outcomes: how supervisory expectations have shifted
Business model and strategy as sources of conduct risk
Lessons from mis-selling and customer redress cases

modules.title: Product Governance
modules.summary: Designing, approving and reviewing products so that they meet the needs of a defined target market and are distributed to the right customers.
objectives: Design a product approval and review process with clear accountability
Define target markets and distribution strategies
Assess existing products against target market needs
syllabus: Product approval committees and governance
Target market definition and testing
Manufacturer and distributor responsibilities
Product reviews, withdrawal and closed-book customers

modules.title: Fair Value and Pricing
modules.summary: Assessing whether the price customers pay is reasonable relative to the benefits they receive, and identifying pricing practices that cause harm.
objectives: Design a fair value assessment methodology
Assess pricing practices, charges and differential treatment of customer groups
Act on fair value findings through product or pricing change
syllabus: Fair value frameworks: price, benefits, costs and quality
Loyalty penalties, price walking and hidden charges
Distribution costs and remuneration in the value chain
Documenting and evidencing fair value assessments

modules.title: Communications and Disclosure
modules.summary: Producing communications that customers actually understand and that support good decisions, and testing their effectiveness.
objectives: Apply clear, fair and not misleading standards to customer communications
Design communication testing to measure customer understanding
Identify behavioural pitfalls such as sludge and choice architecture
syllabus: Financial promotions and disclosure standards
Behavioural insights and choice architecture
Communication testing methods and evidence
Digital journeys, online sales and social media

modules.title: Vulnerable Customers
modules.summary: Identifying customers in vulnerable circumstances, adapting products, services and support, and monitoring whether they achieve outcomes as good as other customers.
objectives: Explain the drivers of vulnerability and how they affect customer decisions
Design processes to identify and support vulnerable customers
Monitor outcomes for vulnerable customers compared with others
syllabus: Drivers of vulnerability: health, life events, resilience and capability
Staff training, recording and data protection
Adjusting products, journeys and support
Outcome monitoring for vulnerable customer groups

modules.title: Sales, Advice and Customer Support
modules.summary: Controlling sales and advice processes so that recommendations are suitable, and providing support that does not create unreasonable barriers for customers.
objectives: Assess sales and advice processes for suitability and pressure selling
Design file reviews and quality assurance for advice
Evaluate customer support journeys for barriers and friction
syllabus: Suitability, appropriateness and execution-only sales
Advice file reviews and quality assurance
Customer support: switching, cancellation and claims
Case study: a sales process under supervisory review

modules.title: Complaints and Root Cause Analysis
modules.summary: Handling complaints fairly and using complaint data to identify and fix the root causes of customer harm across the firm.
objectives: Design a complaints process that delivers fair and timely outcomes
Apply root cause analysis to complaints and other customer data
Identify when wider remediation or redress is required
syllabus: Complaint handling standards and timelines
Root cause analysis techniques
From individual complaints to systemic issues
Customer remediation and redress programmes

modules.title: Outcomes Testing and Management Information
modules.summary: Building outcome testing and management information that show whether customers are being well served, and acting on what the data reveals.
objectives: Design outcome metrics across products, value, understanding and support
Apply outcome testing and data analysis to identify harm
Use management information to drive action rather than reassurance
syllabus: Outcome metrics and indicators of customer harm
Testing methods: data analysis, mystery shopping and file reviews
Data quality and segmentation by customer group
Data exercise: analysing a firm's outcomes data

modules.title: Conduct Risk Frameworks, Culture and Incentives
modules.summary: Embedding conduct risk into the firm's risk framework and aligning culture, remuneration and performance management with good customer outcomes.
objectives: Design a conduct risk framework integrated with the firm's risk management
Assess how culture, incentives and remuneration affect customer outcomes
Apply the three lines model to conduct risk
syllabus: Conduct risk appetite, taxonomy and assessment
Remuneration, sales incentives and performance management
Culture indicators, speak-up and tone from the top
The roles of the business, compliance and internal audit

modules.title: Board Reporting and Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into board reporting that gives directors a clear view of customer outcomes, followed by a workshop in which participants assess their own firm.
objectives: Design board reporting that evidences customer outcomes
Explain how the board should challenge outcome reporting
Produce a prioritised action plan for the firm's conduct risk management
syllabus: The annual board outcomes report
Board challenge and the use of outcome management information
Seeing the firm's customers the way a supervisor does
Workshop: the firm's twelve-month customer outcomes action plan

related.title: Compliance Officer Academy
related.summary: A ten-module academy giving compliance officers the tools to run an independent, risk-based compliance function and handle supervisory engagement with confidence.

related.title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Tracing and Controls for Compliance Teams
related.summary: A nine-module programme equipping compliance teams to detect crypto-asset financial crime, use blockchain analytics, meet travel rule and sanctions obligations, and investigate and report suspicion.

related.title: Financial Crime Compliance in the Age of AI
related.summary: A ten-module programme for MLROs and financial crime teams on the risk-based approach, AI-driven detection, AI-enabled threats and evidencing effectiveness to supervisors.

related.title: Fraud and Scams: Prevention, Detection and Response
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on preventing, detecting and responding to fraud and scams, from authorised push payment scams and deepfakes to reimbursement and board reporting.

related.title: Internal Audit in Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving internal auditors the tools to deliver risk-based assurance over the regulatory risks that matter most to boards and supervisors.

related.title: Internal Investigations and Interviewing Skills
related.summary: A nine-module programme giving control functions a structured method to investigate misconduct, whistleblowing reports and breaches, interview witnesses and subjects, and report findings.
